citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. VIII, pp. 346-410, Figs. 176-193
claim: Isoperimetric/minimal-area principles also govern other hollow and aggregate structures he treats in this chapter (e.g. radiolarian-like and echinoderm larval skeletal arrangements, vessel and tissue partitions).

equations.name: Isoperimetric quotient (circularity)
equations.formula: Q = 4 pi A / P^2  in (0,1]; Q=1 for a circle
equations.role: Pollen grains (Fig. 180), radiolarian central spheres (analogue), hollow shells

equations.name: Hollow sphere surface-to-volume scaling
equations.formula: A = 4 pi r^2, V = 4/3 pi r^3, A/V = 3/r

equations.name: Plateau 120 degree junction
equations.formula: Three cell walls meet at ~120 degrees (360/3)

equations.name: Thompson Fig. 176 eight-sector template
equations.formula: Circle divided into 4 quadrants, each bisected by radial arcs -> 8 equal 45 deg sectors
equations.role: Larval echinoderm skeletal rod arrangement vs Ophiurid pluteus (Fig. 177)

equations.name: Regular tiling isoperimetric excess
equations.formula: P_n^4 / A^2 ordering: hexagon 192 < square 256 < triangle 432 (Thompson Ch. VII link)

equations.name: Kelvin vs Weaire-Phelan foam (counterclaim margin)
equations.formula: Weaire-Phelan beat Kelvin isotropic partition by ~0.3% surface area (1994)
equations.role: Ablation: bulk minimal partition is not unique

parameter_regimes.name: voronoi_disorder_delta
parameter_regimes.role: Froth disorder vs measured tissue junction angles

empirical_claims: Fig. 176 diagrammatic rods match an eight-fold equal-area partition template (Thompson p. 392)
Developing stomata and sporangia (Figs. 178-190) show partitions meeting at ~120 degrees
Radiolarian-like shells are hollow spheres/cages with minimal surface flavour (prose + analogues)
counterclaims: Catch-all claim must be split per structure (Thompson 1917 inventory)
Kelvin minimal foam partition is not globally optimal (Weaire & Phelan 1994, ~0.3% margin)
